answer: Use-it-or-lose-it work receipts. Each identity must submit a signed hash of a unique, non-replayable task output within its window; duplicates collapse to one credit. The registry keeps a relic of each receipt so replay fails. A clone must pay full compute and latency for zero marginal reward, since payouts split across matching hashes. Attackers must harbor separate real work per identity. Cheap cloning hits a reef: the cost per copy stays positive while expected payout trends to zero.
